items.quote: POST /promote, /rollback and /retire, and the MCP promote, rollback and retire tools, never return HTTP 500 or MCP UnexpectedToolError, and never raise AssertionError from promotion._arm_name_for_node_ids, when given a trace token from a partial run.
promote() refuses with a named 422 refusal any trace whose resolved record has partial=true, and writes no ledger row.
An alias whose active ledger row has mutation_id='hipporag' never produces HTTP 500 or MCP UnexpectedToolError.
retire(alias, V) returns 422 ActiveGenerationRetirementError and appends no tombstone when the alias's active record is a rollback whose targets_version equals V.
promote, rollback and retire (engine, REST and MCP) refuse, with a named 422 refusal and no ledger row written, an empty alias and any alias value that the §18.4 Selector refuses at construction.
Ledger connections are closed deterministically, and refused verbs leave the filesystem unchanged.
The ledger exposes an alias-keyed read, for example Ledger.history_for_alias(alias). It returns every row for that alias, oldest first.
The gate verbs promote-next and promote-now are refused before any ledger access, with one named refusal stating that the gate is not calibrated.
POST /trace/resolve and the MCP trace tool accept debug only as a JSON boolean.
Capability selection matches on the effects that the selected wiring actually exercises for the operation, not on the registered Part's maximal effects.
Wiring validation rejects a wiring node whose kind differs from the registered Part.kind for its part reference.
default_registry() contains no admitted part that no selector can reach.
The corpus wiring path layout is defined in one place.
Registry, ledger and selector docstrings match current behaviour.
